## Added

- Optional `pdf-toolkit serve` mode exposes every processing command through
  `POST /v1/run` or `POST /v1/{command}`, returning the CLI's successful JSON
  responses. Existing CLI invocations remain available. Files are read and
  written on the service host; output-producing extraction commands require
  an explicit output path over HTTP.
- Application-controlled lifecycle through `/health`, `/ready`, `/status`,
  `/shutdown`, SIGINT and SIGTERM. Shutdown drains running work for a configurable
  grace period, then terminates and reaps remaining workers. Workers also exit
  if their coordinator dies.
- Configurable concurrency, defaulting to eight disposable CLI workers and
  32 additional request slots. There are no idle worker processes; completed
  jobs release their PDFium, image, geometry and model-client allocations.
  Responses stream from temporary files instead of accumulating in coordinator
  memory.
- Worker memory reservations default to 1 GiB each within an 8 GiB total budget.
  Resident memory is sampled every 100 ms; workers exceeding their limit are
  terminated with a JSON `422` response. Sampling is not a kernel hard cap.
  Rendering is limited to 32 million pixels per page by default, and downsampling
  image-processing batches use at most one quarter of the worker memory limit,
  capped at 256 MiB. Oversized images remain unchanged and count as `too_large`.
- Private loopback binding by default, with bearer authentication required for
  non-loopback listeners. Request bodies, connection counts, execution time and
  stalled response writes have bounded, configurable limits where applicable.
- `ecosystem.config.js` for PM2 start, stop and restart. It reads defaults and
  validates overrides through `serve --print-config`, keeping configuration
  rules in Rust. See [the service guide](../../docs/service.md) for arguments,
  environment variables and integration examples.

## Fixed

- Explicit page lists/ranges cannot expand beyond 65,535 entries, including
  duplicates. Oversized selections are rejected before further allocation.
- Stalled response readers are disconnected after the write idle timeout,
  releasing admission capacity and temporary output files. Unsupported HTTP
  methods and invalid route parameters return the service's JSON error format.
- JSON report output serializes directly to buffered stdout, avoiding an
  intermediate JSON value and a complete serialized string for large reports.

## Changed

- Workspace version 0.16.0, reflected in `docs/json-api.md`. Existing successful
  command response schemas remain unchanged. Service resource limits can reject
  oversized work; explicit page-selection limits also apply to direct CLI calls.
